why: The owner, 2026-10-16: our talk-to NPCs render as Cobblemon's standard (Steve-like) model; 'make him have the correct skin and appearance'. A look is a client NPC variation (assets/<ns>/bedrock/npcs/variations/, docs/research/notes/npc-skins-1.8.md section 2) that tools/client_model_fix.py --server-pack writes into cobblers-client-AllTheMons-subset.zip; tools/compile_dialogue.py gives the NPC's class that resourceIdentifier. The texture is one players already have (the COBBLEVERSE RCTmod RP), so no art is shipped. A player without the subset zip sees the substitute doll for that NPC. Brock's look was seen working in game on 2026-10-16. The owner, 2026-10-20: 'there is still a bunch of steve npcs out there' (Hank and Lena): every NPC with a dialogue class (data/dialogue.json conversations with an npc_id, 108) now has a look, one skin per character (a character with several NPC ids, such as Nia Calder, shares one look), chosen by role, age, gender and place from the 2,010 single/ skins in the COBBLEVERSE RCTmod RP (all 64x64, so all use cobblemon:steve.geo); named canon characters use their named skin (Oak, Sabrina, Brock). Skins the compact-route and HQ trainer records already seat (worker_braden, engineer_bernie, camper_jeff) are avoided. Chosen from the skin file names and the character's lines, not by looking at the textures: a wrong fit is an edit of one 'npcs' entry. Not covered: NPC classes that no conversation opens (the dungeon bosses, stand trainers and egg vendors, tools/dungeon*.py, and the arena classes, tools/arena_runtime.py), which still name cobblemon:standard or no resource.
